# `nish/net/dns-config`

`/etc/resolv.conf` and `/etc/hosts`, read from bytes the caller already has into fixed tables.

```ts
import {
  DNS_CONFIG_MAX_LINE,
  DNS_DEFAULT_ATTEMPTS,
  DNS_DEFAULT_NDOTS,
  DNS_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
  DNS_HOSTS_MAX_ENTRIES,
  DNS_HOSTS_MAX_NAME,
  DNS_HOSTS_MAX_NAMES,
  DNS_HOSTS_MAX_NAME_BYTES,
  DNS_MAX_ATTEMPTS,
  DNS_MAX_NDOTS,
  DNS_MAX_SEARCH,
  DNS_MAX_SEARCH_BYTES,
  DNS_MAX_SERVERS,
  DNS_MAX_TIMEOUT,
  DNS_PORT,
  DnsConfig,
  DnsHosts,
  dnsHostsFind,
  dnsParseAddress,
  dnsParseHosts,
  dnsParseResolvConf,
} from "nish/net/dns-config";
```

```ts
import { DnsConfig, DnsHosts, dnsHostsFind, dnsParseHosts, dnsParseResolvConf } from "nish/net/dns-config"
import { DNS_TYPE_A } from "nish/net/dns-message"

const config: DnsConfig = new DnsConfig()
dnsParseResolvConf(resolvBytes, 0, resolvLen, config)
// config.servers[i * 18, +18) for i < config.serverCount, on port 53
const hosts: DnsHosts = new DnsHosts()
dnsParseHosts(hostsBytes, 0, hostsLen, hosts)
const found: i32 = dnsHostsFind(hosts, "localhost", DNS_TYPE_A, 80, out, 8)
```

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="dnsHostsFind" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#dnshostsfind">

Writes the addresses `hosts` gives `name`, of `qtype` (`DNS_TYPE_A` or `DNS_TYPE_AAAA`), into `out` from offset 0 with `port`, in file order and at most `max` of them, and answers how many it wrote.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="dnsParseAddress" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#dnsparseaddress">

Writes the IPv4 or IPv6 literal `b[off, off + len)` at `out[at, at + 18)`, IPv4 as `::ffff:a.b.c.d`, with `port` big-endian after it, and answers whether it was one.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="dnsParseHosts" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#dnsparsehosts">

Reads the hosts file `b[off, off + len)` into `hosts`, which starts over empty.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="dnsParseResolvConf" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#dnsparseresolvconf">

Reads the resolv.conf `b[off, off + len)` into `config`, which starts over from the defaults, and gives it 127.0.0.1 and ::1 on port 53 when no nameserver line held an address.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="DnsConfig" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#dnsconfig">

One resolv.conf, read by `dnsParseResolvConf`, made once and reusable.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="DnsHosts" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#dnshosts">

One hosts file, read by `dnsParseHosts`, made once and reusable.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-callout type="info">

Both files are local, but neither is trusted to be small or well formed: a
container image, a DHCP client or a VPN writes them, and a resolver that
believed a 40,000-entry search list or a line a megabyte long would spend a
lookup on it. This module reads each into tables of fixed, documented size,
and counts what did not fit rather than growing:

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="resolv.conf">

**resolv.conf** is read as glibc reads it, minus what a stub resolver does
not use. `nameserver` takes one IPv4 or IPv6 literal (no zone), and the first
`DNS_MAX_SERVERS` (3) are kept; `search` and `domain` each replace the list,
so the last one wins, and it holds at most `DNS_MAX_SEARCH` (6) domains and
`DNS_MAX_SEARCH_BYTES` (256) bytes; `options` reads `ndots:n` (clamped to 0
to 15), `timeout:n` (1 to 30 seconds) and `attempts:n` (1 to 5) and ignores
every other option. With no nameserver line, the servers are 127.0.0.1 and
::1, as glibc's are.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="hosts">

**hosts** is an address and then its names, one entry a line. At most
`DNS_HOSTS_MAX_ENTRIES` entries and `DNS_HOSTS_MAX_NAMES` names are kept,
in at most `DNS_HOSTS_MAX_NAME_BYTES` bytes; a name past a cap is dropped and
counted. Names are kept in lowercase and found without case, with one
trailing `.` ignored on either side; an IPv4 address answers only an A
lookup and an IPv6 address only an AAAA one, `::ffff:a.b.c.d` being IPv4.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="In both">

**In both**, `#` and `;` start a comment that runs to the end of the line, a
line no directive names is ignored, and a line longer than
`DNS_CONFIG_MAX_LINE` bytes is skipped whole and counted in
`skippedLines`, never cut to a shorter line that means something else.
A window outside its array is a bug in the caller and panics; nothing in a
file does.

</scalar-detail>

Addresses are the 18-byte form of `docs/LANGUAGE.md`, which
`dnsParseAddress` writes from a literal. The record of what this module
refuses and why is `docs/security/dns.md`.

## dnsHostsFind

Writes the addresses `hosts` gives `name`, of `qtype` (`DNS_TYPE_A` or
`DNS_TYPE_AAAA`), into `out` from offset 0 with `port`, in file order and at
most `max` of them, and answers how many it wrote. An entry that names
`name` twice is written once.

```ts
function dnsHostsFind(
  hosts: DnsHosts,
  name: string,
  qtype: i32,
  port: i32,
  out: u8[],
  max: i32,
): i32
```

## dnsParseAddress

Writes the IPv4 or IPv6 literal `b[off, off + len)` at `out[at, at + 18)`,
IPv4 as `::ffff:a.b.c.d`, with `port` big-endian after it, and answers
whether it was one. `out` is written only when it was. A zone (`%eth0`),
brackets and a port are not part of a literal.

Each call allocates the sixteen bytes it parses into, released when it
returns; the two file parsers reuse a buffer of their own instead.

```ts
function dnsParseAddress(
  b: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
  port: i32,
): boolean
```

## dnsParseResolvConf

Reads the resolv.conf `b[off, off + len)` into `config`, which starts over
from the defaults, and gives it 127.0.0.1 and ::1 on port 53 when no
nameserver line held an address.

```ts
function dnsParseResolvConf(
  b: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
  config: DnsConfig,
): void
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="b" type="u8[]" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="len" type="i32" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="config" type="DnsConfig" required>
</scalar-field>

## DnsConfig

One resolv.conf, read by `dnsParseResolvConf`, made once and reusable.

```ts
class DnsConfig
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new DnsConfig()` |  |
| `attempts: i32` | Rounds through the servers before giving up. |
| `droppedSearch: i32` | Search domains past `DNS_MAX_SEARCH` or `DNS_MAX_SEARCH_BYTES`, read and not kept. |
| `droppedServers: i32` | Nameserver lines past `DNS_MAX_SERVERS`, read and not kept. |
| `ndots: i32` | Dots a name needs to be tried as it stands before the search list. |
| `scratch: u8[]` | Sixteen bytes a literal is parsed into before it is kept, so a parse allocates nothing. |
| `search: u8[]` | The search domains, back to back, lowercase, without a trailing dot. |
| `searchCount: i32` |  |
| `searchLength: i32[]` |  |
| `searchStart: i32[]` | Where each of the `searchCount` domains starts in `search`, and its length. |
| `serverCount: i32` |  |
| `servers: u8[]` | `serverCount` addresses of `DNS_ADDRESS_BYTES` each, on `DNS_PORT`. |
| `skippedLines: i32` | Lines longer than `DNS_CONFIG_MAX_LINE`, skipped whole. |
| `timeout: i32` | Seconds to wait for one server's reply. |

## DnsHosts

One hosts file, read by `dnsParseHosts`, made once and reusable.

```ts
class DnsHosts
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new DnsHosts()` |  |
| `addresses: u8[]` | `entryCount` addresses of `DNS_ADDRESS_BYTES` each, port 0. |
| `droppedEntries: i32` | Lines with an address past `DNS_HOSTS_MAX_ENTRIES`, read and not kept. |
| `droppedNames: i32` | Names past a cap, or longer than `DNS_HOSTS_MAX_NAME`, read and not kept. |
| `entryCount: i32` |  |
| `nameBytes: i32` |  |
| `nameCount: i32` |  |
| `nameEntry: i32[]` |  |
| `nameLength: i32[]` |  |
| `names: u8[]` | Every kept name, back to back, lowercase, without a trailing dot. |
| `nameStart: i32[]` | Where each of the `nameCount` names starts in `names`, its length, and its entry. |
| `scratch: u8[]` | Sixteen bytes a literal is parsed into before it is kept, so a parse allocates nothing. |
| `skippedLines: i32` | Lines longer than `DNS_CONFIG_MAX_LINE`, skipped whole. |

## Limits

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="1,024" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DNS_CONFIG_MAX_LINE: i32`

The longest line either parser reads; a longer one is skipped whole.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="256" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DNS_HOSTS_MAX_ENTRIES: i32`

How many hosts lines are kept.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="253" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DNS_HOSTS_MAX_NAME: i32`

The longest hosts name kept, the longest a DNS name can be.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1,024" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DNS_HOSTS_MAX_NAMES: i32`

How many names all hosts entries may hold together.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="16,384" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DNS_HOSTS_MAX_NAME_BYTES: i32`

How many bytes those names may take together.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DNS_MAX_ATTEMPTS: i32`

The highest `attempts:n` kept; the lowest is 1.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="15" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DNS_MAX_NDOTS: i32`

The highest `ndots:n` kept; a higher one is clamped to it, as glibc clamps.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DNS_MAX_SEARCH: i32`

How many search domains are kept.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="256" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DNS_MAX_SEARCH_BYTES: i32`

How many bytes the search domains may take together.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DNS_MAX_SERVERS: i32`

How many `nameserver` lines are kept; glibc's MAXNS.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="30" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DNS_MAX_TIMEOUT: i32`

The highest `timeout:n` kept, in seconds; the lowest is 1.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
